events.title: Nuremberg Trials Begin
events.description: The International Military Tribunal opened in Nuremberg, Germany, to try 24 leading Nazi officials for war crimes, crimes against humanity, crimes against peace, and conspiracy. Proceedings were held in the Palace of Justice.
events.significance: The trials established key precedents in international criminal law, including the principle that individuals, including heads of state and military leaders, can be held accountable for atrocities, and influenced the later creation of the International Criminal Court.

events.title: Microsoft Releases Windows 1.0
events.description: Microsoft released Windows 1.0, its first graphical user interface-based operating environment for personal computers, running on top of MS-DOS and featuring tiled windows, menus, and mouse support.
events.significance: Windows 1.0 marked the beginning of the Windows product line, which became the dominant desktop operating system worldwide and shaped the personal computing industry for decades.

events.title: UN General Assembly Adopts the Convention on the Rights of the Child
events.description: The United Nations General Assembly unanimously adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child, setting out civil, political, economic, social, health, and cultural rights for children.
events.significance: It became the most widely ratified human rights treaty in history and established international standards for child protection, now commemorated annually as World Children's Day on November 20.

events.title: Launch of the Zarya Module of the International Space Station
events.description: Russia launched the Zarya Functional Cargo Block from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan aboard a Proton rocket, providing the first component of the International Space Station.
events.significance: This launch began the assembly of the ISS, the largest international scientific cooperation project in space, which has been continuously inhabited since November 2000.

events.title: Mexican Revolution Begins
events.description: Francisco I. Madero's Plan de San Luis Potosí called for an uprising against President Porfirio Díaz on this date, launching the Mexican Revolution.
events.significance: The revolution ended Díaz's long rule and led to major political and social change in Mexico, including the Constitution of 1917. The date is a national holiday in Mexico.
